description: Settling a village apart (core src/editor/layout/settle.ts and pairing.ts; the Unreal plugin's BYOA B7 r4 - B8 r5 settle, characterised from its Portable code). The smallest change that parts what stands too close: each pair short of the gap its rule asks, and each body inside its clearance of an obstacle, pushed apart along the axis that separates them most, the lighter taking the larger share, repeated until nothing is short or nothing can move, every body within its own limit; shifts quantized to the millimetre. The neighbour rule (fitted buildings: the larger of two gaps, 0.25 m off other lots' paving, a limit that grows with the gap) on Brightwater Vale's ring of seven pack houses at 1, 4.5 and 6 m and on its real fits; the clearance rule (props out of each other and the walls, plant trunks off walls and paving, set-asides) on its props, whose positions and archetypes are the world's and at the sizes the editor measured (by entity id where the editor's build stood the prop, else its archetype's measured size); the player start's clear ground (startClearRadiusM, 1 m round the IR's player.startPosition: a prop or plant the settle left on it moved off by the least move, a building on it named, set-asides read where the items end); the pairing's seat sink; and the rules' tables. Plan frame: IR (x, z) metres.

sources.measuredBy: the Unreal editor at unreal 86857a0 (P0.unreal.u23-boxes round 1, WV0 run 2, 2026-11-05): the 36 GB Mac's tools/probe_u23.py over the paired level PairedBrightwater. The houses as building-fit.json's source says (House_03's bottom -5.3567 m, BP_House_02's: its seat sink 0.72, was 0.81). Each clearance prop's plan length (its own forward axis), depth and height are CalculateComponentsBoundingBoxInLocalSpace over its colliding primitives times |scale|, to the centimetre as standins.txt states them (19 archetypes, e.g. barrel 0.71 x 0.73 x 0.99, lantern 0.24 x 0.97 x 2.92, bench 0.55 x 1.85 x 0.62, well 1.64 x 2.07 x 2.31, where the nominal sizes by kind were 0.6 x 0.6 x 0.9, 0.3 x 0.3 x 2.6, 1.6 x 0.5 x 0.5 and 1.6 x 1.6 x 1.2): 73 of the 85 props by their own entity id; the 12 the editor's newer world export did not stand (an anvil and 11 walls) by their archetype's measured size (anvil 0.33 x 0.35 x 0.48; wall 2.00 x 0.14 x 1.52, the more often measured of its two). Each prop keeps its characterised centre and axes
